standard.title: Rehearse and perform drama
standard.description: rehearse and perform improvised, devised and/or scripted drama to audiences, using performance skills and conventions relevant to style and/or form
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform drama for an audience with basic performance skills (AC9ADR6P01). They have not yet used deliberate rehearsal strategies, systematically collected audience feedback, or reflected on the relationship between intention and audience reception.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and perform drama for audiences using performance skills and conventions appropriate to style and form, reflecting on the relationship between intention and audience reception.

nodes.label: Rehearsing with performance intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the rehearsal process to develop performance readiness — technical skills, conventions and expressive clarity — with a clear sense of intended audience experience
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearse drama with at least one clear performance goal; explain what the rehearsal developed and how it affects the audience experience
nodes.typical_width: Plan and use rehearsal to develop performance readiness across technical skills, conventions and expressive clarity; use Viewpoints questions to evaluate rehearsal progress; document decisions
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to set and evaluate rehearsal goals — 'What are our intentions?', 'Is meaning clear?', 'Is it engaging?' — develop these as ongoing rehearsal tools rather than post-performance reflection
Use video to review own rehearsal performance — evaluate what the recording reveals that in-the-moment rehearsal misses
Develop rehearsal strategies that systematically address specific performance challenges — evaluate the strategies' effectiveness over multiple sessions

response_modes.reason: Purposeful rehearsal — using targeted strategies to address specific performance challenges — is a disciplined habit that develops through repeated cycles. Students who simply run through material repeatedly without targeted evaluation don't develop the rehearsal discipline that makes performance improve.

success_criteria: Rehearses with at least one clear performance goal
Explains what the rehearsal developed and how it affects audience experience
Rehearsal is targeted — not just running through material

nodes.label: Performing with style-appropriate skills and conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform drama using performance skills and conventions relevant to the style or form with clear communicative intent
nodes.minimum_width: Perform drama using at least one performance skill and one convention relevant to the style or form; explain how each serves the intended dramatic communication
nodes.typical_width: Perform improvised, devised or scripted drama using performance skills and conventions appropriate to the style; suit choices to the underlying dramatic structure; demonstrate communicative intent throughout
wider: Perform using conventions that match the underlying dramatic structure — evaluate how structural choices constrain and enable performance decisions

Perform drama that explores First Nations Australian perspectives on identity, resilience or environmental practices — apply ICIP responsibilities and communicate with respectful and empathetic intent
Develop performance choices that demonstrate genuine empathy for the characters and situations portrayed — evaluate how empathy is expressed through performance skills rather than just described

response_modes.reason: Students commonly perform using familiar skills without reasoning through whether those choices serve the style or the intended communication. Scaffolding the reasoning — what does this style/form require, what performance skill or convention serves that, am I making choices that communicate to the audience or just demonstrating what I can do — builds purposeful performance thinking.

success_criteria: Uses at least one performance skill and one convention appropriate to the style
Choices are connected to communicative intent — not just demonstrations of ability
Performance demonstrates empathy and appropriate respect for material and audience

nodes.label: Evaluating performance and audience reception
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect and evaluate audience feedback and reflect on whether performance communicated intended meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on whether the performance communicated the intended meaning; identify at least one thing that worked and one that would change
nodes.typical_width: Collect and evaluate audience feedback; use Viewpoints questions to reflect on intentions, clarity and engagement; evaluate the gap between intention and reception; document how the evaluation would inform future performance
wider: Collect audience feedback systematically — compare audience reception with own intentions and evaluate the gap between what was communicated and what was intended
Reflect on how respectful relationships and empathy were expressed in performance and interpreted by the audience — evaluate whether the audience received the intended empathetic portrayal

Use Viewpoints questions as reflective tools — 'What were your intentions?', 'Was meaning clear?', 'What audience response suggested it was engaging?' — evaluate what each question reveals about the performance

response_modes.reason: This node integrates rehearsal preparation (Node 1), purposeful performance (Node 2), and feedback-based reflection from D02 into a complete performance event and evaluation cycle. Students who can perform but cannot evaluate the relationship between intention and audience reception have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Reflects on whether intended meaning was communicated to the audience
Identifies at least one specific aspect that worked and one that would change
Evaluation addresses the gap between intention and audience reception
